1. [P0] | A2’s “one route per rack instance” contradicts the locked NVL576 invariant it promises to preserve. | Evidence: [plan:36](/Users/caoruixin/.claude/plans/the-goal-toasty-charm.md:36) expands every cluster route folded onto an eight-instance rack; `con.ru.optics-interrack` has exactly that shape at [rubin-ultra-nvl576.ts:856](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/data/rubin-ultra-nvl576.ts:856), while [routing.test.ts:93](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/lib/routing.test.ts:93) requires exactly one semantic route. | Why it matters: returning eight routes fails the locked test; suffixing `connectionId` also breaks flow lookup because [routing.ts:225](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/lib/routing.ts:225) indexes by content connection ID. | Concrete suggested fix: preserve one `RoutedConnection` per content connection and attach separately keyed instance paths, or expand geometry only in the render layer while keeping `connectionId` unchanged.

2. [P1] | A single stored `flow.activeAssemblyIds`, updated only on step changes, cannot correctly serve both exact hardware chips and LOD-collapsed scene highlights. | Evidence: [plan:47](/Users/caoruixin/.claude/plans/the-goal-toasty-charm.md:47) collapses only connection endpoints and leaves `highlightAssemblyIds` exact; KV-write contains only HBM and Grace IDs at [flows.ts:87](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/data/flows.ts:87), which are not mounted at cluster/rack depth, while navigation changes depth independently of `setFlow`. | Why it matters: KV-write can have no glowing hardware at rack/cluster level, and stored IDs become stale after drilling or changing generation. | Concrete suggested fix: derive two sets from `{system, episode, step, depth}`—exact referenced IDs for chips and every ID collapsed through `visibleAncestorAt` for scene highlighting—rather than storing derived IDs in Zustand.

3. [P1] | The plan leaves board-level flow paths and beacons in compact coordinates while the hardware is rendered exploded. | Evidence: board rendering passes `exploded` into `AssemblyBranch` at [SceneRoot.tsx:430](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/SceneRoot.tsx:430), but `ConnectionLayer` receives only depth at [SceneRoot.tsx:527](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/SceneRoot.tsx:527); routing defaults `exploded=false` at [routing.ts:186](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/lib/routing.ts:186), and FlowLayer uses that default at [FlowLayer.tsx:54](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/FlowLayer.tsx:54) plus hard-coded `false` for HBM at [FlowLayer.tsx:114](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/FlowLayer.tsx:114). | Why it matters: thicker lines, particles, and portal stubs will still be visibly detached from exploded hardware. | Concrete suggested fix: pass the actual `level`/`exploded` state to both layers and use it consistently in routing and `worldPositionOf`.

4. [P1] | B4 does not define the necessary incident-route filtering or the correct rendered subtree for portal stubs. | Evidence: [routing.ts:189](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/lib/routing.ts:189) currently routes every system connection; at board level the focus may be a GPU, but [SceneRoot.tsx:515](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/SceneRoot.tsx:515) renders its containing tray. | Why it matters: routes with neither endpoint in the displayed tray can remain as room-spanning lines, while using the raw board focus can incorrectly stub links between two visible tray components. | Concrete suggested fix: pass the rendered scene anchor (`anchor.trayAssemblyId`), keep full routes when both endpoints are inside it, create one stub when exactly one is inside, and drop routes when neither is inside.

5. [P1] | C1’s proposed effect split would leave camera distance clamps stale after navigation. | Evidence: [plan:62](/Users/caoruixin/.claude/plans/the-goal-toasty-charm.md:62) assigns clamp updates to an effect depending only on width/height, whereas the current clamps are recalculated alongside level/focus/generation at [CameraRig.tsx:53](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/CameraRig.tsx:53). | Why it matters: drilling from cluster to board can retain cluster-scale min/max distances, permitting unusable zoom ranges. | Concrete suggested fix: memoize the preset from navigation state plus aspect; the navigation effect should update clamps and `setLookAt`, while the resize effect updates clamps and conditionally refits only when `userMoved` is false.

6. [P1] | The proposed camera E2E assertion can pass even when the camera really resets. | Evidence: [plan:71](/Users/caoruixin/.claude/plans/the-goal-toasty-charm.md:71) only requires the post-click screenshot to differ from a default baseline, but clicking a step already changes line width/opacity at [ConnectionLayer.tsx:90](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/ConnectionLayer.tsx:90), and the plan adds further hardware highlights. | Why it matters: a reset default camera plus changed flow pixels still differs from the default baseline; resizing also changes image dimensions trivially. | Concrete suggested fix: assert camera position/target before versus after the click and resize through minimal test telemetry, and separately assert that the canvas bounding-box height stays constant across step changes.

7. [P1] | The proposed cluster/rack HBM beacon scaling is incompatible with the existing beacon visibility and instance model. | Evidence: HBM positions are explicitly suppressed below tray depth at [FlowLayer.tsx:107](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/FlowLayer.tsx:107); if that guard is removed, [FlowLayer.tsx:109](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/FlowLayer.tsx:109) produces one position per assembly type and [FlowLayer.tsx:114](/Users/caoruixin/projects/aifactory/src/components/scene/FlowLayer.tsx:114) selects instance 0. | Why it matters: the advertised cluster/rack multipliers are either dead code or place one misleading HBM dot on only the first rack. | Concrete suggested fix: keep HBM beacons only where HBM meshes are actually rendered and use collapsed assembly highlighting at coarse LODs; scale moving particles independently.
